summary.headline: EPL Q4 FY26 revenue grew 17.6% with EBITDA margin at 20.2%; FY26 revenue up 13% and margin 20.4%, alongside proposed Indovida merger.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 17.6% YoY, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth, with growth broad-based across all four regions. EBITDA rose 17.2% with margin at 20.2%, and PAT excluding exceptional items rose about 1%, while full-year PAT grew 15%. Beauty & Cosmetics grew 30% and Oral Care recovered to 10% growth. Management said the Middle East crisis is raising raw material and logistics costs, which it expects to fully pass through, and it announced a proposed merger with Indovida.

financial_highlights.change: Highest in last 5 years; fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Seventh consecutive quarter at or above 20%

segments.name: Beauty & Cosmetics (B&C)
segments.commentary: Grew a record 30% YoY in Q4 and 30% for FY26, with fourth consecutive quarter above 20%; B&C now 40% of business and larger than Oral Care in most key markets.

segments.name: Oral Care
segments.commentary: Grew 10% YoY in Q4 after FY25 headwinds; 47% of business. Management expects oral to deliver as expected in FY27.

segments.name: EAP (East Asia Pacific)
segments.commentary: Grew 25% YoY, mainly driven by China per management; Thailand plant (set up November) contributed little volume this quarter.

segments.name: Americas
segments.commentary: Grew 24.1% YoY; US, Mexico, Colombia and Brazil each grew double digits, with Brazil a standout.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 15.5% YoY, attributed to strong category performance across markets.

segments.name: AMESA
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.4% YoY, but EBITDA grew about 1% and EBIT fell about 11%; management cited CEO transition costs and a high base from last year's phasing reversal. FY26 AMESA margin 18.7% vs 18.5%.

segments.name: India standalone
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 11.5% YoY, driven by B&C and an Oral Care recovery.

guidance_outlook: Long-term guidance unchanged: revenue growth of 11%-13% consistently, with EBITDA growth slightly ahead of revenue growth.
Management said cost inflation from the Middle East crisis cannot be included in steady-state guidance and may show up temporarily over a quarter or two.
Management expects to recover all additional crisis-related costs, with no expected lag even for non-contractual customers.
Raw material availability is secured until at least mid-July 2026, with inventory extended weekly.
Capex to stay at a slightly elevated level in FY27 as the company captures market share; capex will be phased but not constrained for growth.
Thailand volumes expected to start in the next couple of quarters of FY27 and scale gradually.
Merger completion expected by Q4 FY27 (about 12 months from end-March announcement); dividend payout to resume after merger, and no dividend declared until then.
Merger regulatory approval expected within about one year of filing; SEBI and CCI approvals already filed.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex of INR 480+ crores, mostly directed at Beauty & Cosmetics (capacity, innovation, back-end flexibility, extrusion).
Capex is running ahead of depreciation (INR 480 crores vs INR 385 crores) and will be phased to approach depreciation over time.
Thailand greenfield plant set up in November 2025 at about $5 million; in validation and customer certification, with little volume in FY26 numbers.
Large equipment capitalised in Q4 drove the sequential rise in depreciation.
Organic growth capex is funded internally; company remains actively seeking acquisitions in B&C that add geography or capability and are growth and margin accretive.
demand_pricing: Pass-through model is now landed cost plus power; nearly 50% (management also said more than 50%) of business is under contractual pass-through, with proactive price increases for other customers.
Pricing is reviewed on a customer-wise gross contribution basis monthly, and management says it now operates on weekly or more frequent cadence during the crisis.
Management said the Middle East crisis did not materially affect Q4 volumes; growth attributed to B&C momentum and oral recovery.
Management believes the company's supplier relationships and scale give it competitive advantage and potential market share gains.
Management declined to quantify blended raw material inflation, saying it varies by region and changes weekly.
Brazil described as a standout performer after three years of presence; Thailand expected to follow a similar path.

qa_highlights.question: How is EPL positioned to handle cost inflation, and how far can margins fall versus the 2023-24 squeeze?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply is secured to mid-July and costs will be fully recovered, but gave no margin floor, saying there may be optical margin changes.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 17.5% revenue growth driven by pricing, inventory push, or one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs; growth came from B&C (+30%) and oral (+10%), with China as the main EAP driver and Brazil leading Americas.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance only 11%-13% when inflation and Thailand could support higher growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 11%-13% is a long-term guide, quarters may vary with pricing, and inflation is excluded from steady-state guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AMESA EBITDA and EBIT fall despite 10% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Goyal attributed it to two CEO transition costs and a high base from last year's phasing reversal; on a normalised basis margins are in target range, and FY26 AMESA margin rose to 18.7%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no dividend and what is the merger timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: No dividend because of the share swap merger; merger expected by Q4 FY27 subject to approvals, with dividend policy to be set by the Board after completion.

qa_highlights.question: Are acquisitions still being pursued given accumulating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively seeking acquisitions in B&C that add geography or capability; dividend policy has no material impact on that, and debt-free Indovida would add capacity.

risks_watch: Middle East crisis: raw material availability and cost inflation, with recovery timing and margin optics for non-contractual customers.
AMESA profitability: EBITDA and EBIT did not track 10% revenue growth in Q4; watch whether the normalisation claim holds in Q1 FY27.
Thailand plant ramp-up: volumes expected from the next couple of quarters of FY27.
Merger timing and approvals (SEBI, CCI, antitrust in multiple countries); timeline could extend beyond Q4 FY27.
Capex running above depreciation and possible margin drag from continued B&C investment in front-end, innovation and back-end.
Oral Care recovery sustainability after FY25 headwinds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, pass-through and the merger, but guarded on margins and inflation; management repeatedly declined to quantify the margin trough or blended inflation and deflected some EBIT and AMESA questions to full-year figures.
key_quotes: This is the highest ever revenue growth in the last 5 years.
We remain confident of delivering robust absolute EBITDA growth.
we will recover all the additional costs, which comes on account of this crisis.
Steady state, I expect our tax rates to be in the range of 18% to 22%.

rows.label: Indovida merger (share swap), completion by Q4 FY27
